steps.observation:
[Search] Results for 'When was Harry Bowen born?':
[Doc 1] Harry Bowen (actor): Harry Bowen (October 4, 1888 – December 5, 1941) was an American character actor of the silent and sound film eras.

[Doc 2] Harry Bowen (actor):  Born on October 4, 1888 in Brooklyn, New York, he broke into the film industry doing film shorts during the silent era.

[Doc 3] Harry Bowen (actor):  Other notable films in which he appeared include: the 1933 classic "King Kong"; "Flying Down to Rio" (1933), which was the first on-screen pairing of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers; John Ford's 1935 comedy, "The Whole Town's Talking", starring Edward G. Robinson; and "Next Time We Love" (1936), starring Margaret Sullavan, James Stewart, and Ray Milland.

[Doc 4] Harry Bowen (actor):  His work on shorts continued into talking pictures, and it was in 1929 that he made his first appearance in a full-length feature, with a small role in "Red Hot Rhythm", directed by Leo McCarey.

[Doc 5] Harry Bowen (actor):  His final screen performance, according to AFI, was the 1939 film, "The Day the Bookies Wept", starring Joe Penner and Betty Grable.
